Senses.Note: The verdict belongs to an encounter and can be reversed: a person who claims to have exposed another may in turn be declared exposed.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The compound marks a test carried through to exposure: to see someone or something through.
EvidenceBody: Zhaozhou Congshen returns from testing the old woman on the road to Mount Wutai and declares that he has seen her through. Xuedou Chongxian and Wansong Xingxiu use the completed formula as a capping verdict. Dahui Zonggao turns it reflexively, telling an interlocutor that the old monk has been seen through by him before striking when he hesitates. Another transmitted version gives Zhaozhou's declaration that he saw the woman through. Wumen Huikai reverses the testing relation by saying the two hermits instead saw Zhaozhou through, and elsewhere preserves Zhaozhou's declaration in the Wutai-woman case. The tester can thus be tested in turn; the verb denotes successful exposure claimed within the encounter, not an infallible external judgment.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: The compound marks a test carried through to exposure: to see someone or something through.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: Wumen reverses the familiar testing relation and says that the two hermits saw Zhaozhou through; the phrase therefore records a claimed outcome within the case, not an infallible external judgment.
